Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement (synthetic test fixture)

Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a moderate pace. Job gains have slowed, and the unemployment rate has edged up but remains low. Inflation has moved down over the past year but remains somewhat elevated relative to the Committee's two percent objective.

The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate. In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.

The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities. The balance sheet runoff will proceed at the pace previously announced. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.

Voting for the monetary policy action were all members of the Committee present at the meeting, and the decision was unanimous.

Last Update: November 4, 2026. Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System.
